usageNotes: Use this to enumerate all Ceph pools in a managed cluster and inspect their replication settings, PG counts, and current usage. The `cluster` path parameter must be the Ceph FSID (not a friendly name), which can be retrieved from `get_ceph_clusters`. Usage statistics (`bytes_used`, `percent_used`) are optional and will be absent if the cluster has not yet reported them.

examples.summary: List all pools in a Ceph cluster by FSID

tips: The `cluster` value is the Ceph FSID (UUID format), not a human-readable cluster name — use get_ceph_clusters to look it up first.
Pool type 'unknown' means PDM does not recognise the pool type; treat those pools as read-only/opaque.
When pg_autoscale_mode is 'on', the live pg_num may drift from pg_num_final as the autoscaler adjusts — compare both fields to detect in-progress scaling.
application_metadata keys (e.g. 'rbd', 'cephfs', 'rgw') indicate which Ceph service is using the pool; pools with no application tag are unassigned.
